# dsh-agent-browser
English | 中文

Let the model actually **use** the DSH right-Sidebar browser: read a page's text,
click and type in

it, navigate, size the viewport, and take screenshots — from

It also adds a **phone / tablet / desktop / custom viewport switcher**, so you can
see how a site re
nders at another size without leaving the app.

> **Desktop only.** The tools drive an Electron `<webview>` guest. In Web
> profiles the Sidebar bro

wser is a sandboxed cross-origin `<iframe>`, whose DOM
> cannot be read at all, so the tools answer

with an explicit reason naming the
> Web profile instead of pretending to work. `browser_tabs` still

lists those
> tabs — as `mounted: true` with `carrier: "iframe"` — so you can see that the

ists and why it cannot be driven.

> **Third-party, non-invasive plugin.** It mounts from your DSH profile, never
> touches `app.asar`,
and leaves the built-in browser exactly as shipped.

### How it works, and why not zoom

The guest is an Electron `<webview>`, and that element's box **is** the page's
viewport: a 390px-wid

e element makes the document lay out at 390 CSS pixels. To
show a viewport wider than the column, th

e element is scaled down for display
only, inside a clipping container, and the scale is recomputed

tation shrinks. `pageWidth` in the read-back is the guest's own
`window.innerWidth`, so it always re
ports what the page believes.

`<webview>.setZoomFactor()` is deliberately **not** used. Chromium's zoom policy
is same-origin, so

zooming one tab would also zoom any other tab showing the same
site — tabs in one workspace share a

storage partition. Element box plus a CSS
transform keeps every tab independent.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Two design choices worth knowing:

- **The Inspect channel, not a private transport.** `cordisInspect` is the
one first-class Host→Clie

nt request/response mechanism: it correlates by
requestId, honours the tool call's `AbortSignal`, an

d validates input and
output against declared JSON schemas. Reusing it means no new wire protocol.
-

**The page is driven through its own carrier.** Each page-side helper is
serialized with `toString(

)` and wrapped in a single IIFE before
`executeJavaScript`, so the helpers see each other without to

uching the
visited page's globals.

The provider reads `[data-sidebar-right-tab]` inside
`[data-sidebar-right-session]` to map a tab to

its guest. Desktop browser tabs
declare `keepMounted`, so a tab keeps its DOM across tab switches, S

ession
switches, collapse and floating — which is what lets a tool reach a tab the user

## Known limitations

- **Desktop only**, as above.
- **Mounted tabs only.** A tab that is open but not yet mounted cannot

be
driven; the tool says so and asks you to click that tab once. (In practice
tabs mount as soon as

they are opened or restored.) Setting a viewport is the
exception: it is stored and applied when th

e tab mounts.
- **Opening a tab needs this Conversation's Sidebar to have a surface.** The
Session-a

ddressed open is a silent no-op for a Session whose Sidebar store has
never been adopted, so `browse

r_navigate` without a `tabId` can fail with "not
created" in a Conversation that has never shown its

right Sidebar. Open that
Conversation's Sidebar once and retry. Navigating an existing tab is unaff

ected.
- **`shortcuts.register` requires a `defaults` map.** Omitting it throws during
`apply()`, wh

ich takes down the entire client half — the Inspect provider
included — and surfaces only as `web bo

ot: … did not activate`. This plugin
ships `defaults: {}`; `test/apply-check.cjs` guards the shape s

o the outage
cannot come back silently.
- **The menu item reads `sessionId` from a standard slot pro

p.** It falls back to
the enclosing `[data-sidebar-right-session]` only if a future shell stops
prov

iding it, so the control keeps working either way.
- **The tab menu is a right-click menu, not a "⋯"

button.** The kit's tab strip
has no overflow button; the menu is opened by the tab's `onContextMen

u`
handler. `Modal` is deliberately **not** used for the custom-size form: the kit
dismisses the men

u on any `pointerdown` outside its own element, and `Modal`
portals to `document.body`, so a portale

d dialog would destroy itself on first
click. The form renders inline and stops pointer events inste

ad.
- **`jsx(type, props, key)` takes the React KEY third — not children.** This
plugin shipped a bu

g from exactly that: labels were passed as the third
argument, which compiles and renders *empty* bu

ttons (the live menu showed six
blank rows). Children always go in `props.children`.
`test/apply-che

ck.cjs` asserts every menu item carries a non-empty label.

one slot scope.** Declaring `store` on

### Requirements

- **Desktop app only.** The tools drive an Electron `<webview>` guest. Web
profiles render a sandbox

ed cross-origin `<iframe>` whose DOM cannot be read,
so the tools report an explicit reason instead

of pretending to work.
- **DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`** is the version this is verified against. The plugin re

lies
on public contracts (the Inspect provider registry, the
`sidebar.right.tab.menu.item` and `sett

ings.general.item` seats, and the
`[data-sidebar-right-*]` DOM attributes), so it should survive pat

ch updates —
but see *Compatibility* for how that was checked, and *Known limitations* for
what happ

ens if a contract moves.
- **Node 20+** to run the test suite.
## Compatibility

The plugin was written against an earlier DSH and has since been re-verified
against **`0.2.1-rc.2`*

*. Nothing needed changing to keep working; one new
harness extension point was adopted.
